## 1. New LLM Versions / Major AI Lab Tools

- **Date:** 2026-04-22  
  **Link:** [OpenAI — Introducing workspace agents in ChatGPT](https://openai.com/index/introducing-workspace-agents-in-chatgpt/)  
  **Summary:** OpenAI introduced Codex-powered workspace agents for ChatGPT Business, Enterprise, Edu, and Teachers in research preview. The agents can use connected tools, run on schedules, operate in Slack, request approvals for sensitive actions, and expose admin analytics.  
  **Why it matters:** OpenAI is moving Codex from individual coding assistance toward managed enterprise automation with governance controls.

- **Date:** 2026-04-22  
  **Link:** [OpenAI — Making ChatGPT better for clinicians](https://openai.com/index/making-chatgpt-better-for-clinicians/)  
  **Summary:** OpenAI launched ChatGPT for Clinicians, free for verified U.S. physicians, nurse practitioners, physician assistants, and pharmacists. It adds clinical search, deep research across medical journals, reusable clinical workflow skills, CME support, and HealthBench Professional.  
  **Why it matters:** This is a targeted vertical product move into regulated clinical workflows, with identity verification and domain-specific evaluation.

- **Date:** 2026-04-22  
  **Link:** [Google — Cloud Next ’26: Momentum and innovation at Google scale](https://blog.google/innovation-and-ai/infrastructure-and-cloud/google-cloud/cloud-next-2026-sundar-pichai/)  
  **Summary:** Google announced Gemini Enterprise Agent Platform at Cloud Next ’26.  
  **Why it matters:** Google is positioning Gemini as an enterprise agent platform, not only a model layer.

- **Date:** 2026-04-22  
  **Link:** [Alibaba Cloud — Qwen3.6-Max-Preview](https://www.alibabacloud.com/blog/603055)  
  **Summary:** Alibaba/Qwen previewed Qwen3.6-Max-Preview, a proprietary hosted model positioned above Qwen3.6-Plus, emphasizing agentic coding, instruction following, world knowledge, and real-world agent reliability.  
  **Why it matters:** Qwen is continuing to compete in closed frontier-style hosted models, especially for coding and agent workloads.

- **Date:** 2026-04-21  
  **Link:** [OpenAI — Introducing ChatGPT Images 2.0](https://openai.com/index/introducing-chatgpt-images-2-0)  
  **Summary:** OpenAI introduced ChatGPT Images 2.0, citing improved text rendering, multilingual support, and visual reasoning.  
  **Why it matters:** Image generation remains a frontier capability area; text rendering and multilingual visual output are practical adoption constraints.

- **Date:** 2026-04-21  
  **Link:** [OpenAI — Scaling Codex to enterprises worldwide](https://openai.com/index/scaling-codex-to-enterprises-worldwide)  
  **Summary:** OpenAI announced Codex Labs and enterprise deployment partnerships with Accenture, PwC, Infosys, and others; it also reported 4M Codex weekly active users.  
  **Why it matters:** Codex is being pushed as an enterprise software-development platform, with systems integrators positioned as deployment channels.

## 2. FOSS / Open-Weight LMs & Tools

- **Date:** 2026-04-22  
  **Link:** [OpenAI — Introducing OpenAI Privacy Filter](https://openai.com/index/introducing-openai-privacy-filter/)  
  **Summary:** OpenAI released Privacy Filter, an Apache-2.0 open-weight model for detecting and redacting PII in text. It is designed for local, high-throughput privacy workflows and long inputs.  
  **Why it matters:** OpenAI is releasing a narrow open-weight model for enterprise privacy infrastructure, where local deployment and auditability matter.

- **Date:** 2026-04-22  
  **Link:** [Kimi — Kimi K2.6 Pricing for API and Membership](https://www.kimi.com/resources/kimi-k2-6-pricing)  
  **Summary:** Moonshot AI published pricing and availability details for Kimi K2.6, described as an open-source model for coding, long-horizon execution, and agent-swarm workflows, with a listed 262,144-token context window.  
  **Why it matters:** Long-context open-weight coding models are becoming commercially packaged for agentic execution, not just benchmark release.
